quick_skim.title: Koopman Spectral Analysis of Lithium-Ion Battery Dynamics: State of Charge as a Marginally Stable Observable
quick_skim.abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation remains a fundamental challenge in lithium-ion battery management systems because battery dynamics are highly nonlinear, operating-condition dependent, and sensitive to parameter variations caused by aging and temperature. Conventional model-based estimators, such as equivalent circuit model (ECM) and Kalman-filter-based approaches, rely heavily on repeated parameter identification and accurate electrochemical modeling, whereas purely data-driven methods often sacrifice physical interpretability.   This work proposes a Koopman-theoretic, data-driven framework for SOC estimation using Dynamic Mode Decomposition with control (DMDc) combined with Hankel time-delay embedding. Instead of explicitly identifying ECM parameters, the proposed approach reconstructs a lifted dynamical state space directly from measured terminal voltage and current obtained through Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC) testing. Spectral decomposition of the identified DMDc operator reveals intrinsic battery dynamics in terms of Koopman modes and eigenvalues. The SOC dynamics naturally emerge as the slowest marginally stable mode whose eigenvalue lies closest to the unit circle, consistent with the integrator-type behavior of charge conservation. The corresponding modal coordinate is subsequently utilized as an SOC-sensitive observable.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Proposes a Koopman-theoretic framework for SOC estimation using DMDc and Hankel embedding, achieving accurate and interpretable SOC estimation without repeated parameter identification, relevant for UAV battery management.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对锂离子电池SOC估计因非线性和老化而困难的挑战，提出基于Koopman理论和动态模态分解的数据驱动框架，结合汉克尔时延嵌入，实现无需重复参数辨识的高精度SOC估计。实验证明该方法在多种工况下优于传统等效电路模型和卡尔曼滤波方法，为无人机电池管理提供了物理可解释且鲁棒的解决方案。
